v.why: Very large L2 penalties cause severe underfitting, so relaxing them yields big gains (probes 3, 16).
Increasing an already strong penalty pushes the network further into underfitting.
Tiny learning rates leave training unconverged within 243 epochs, so increasing them helps (probes 62, 73).
Raising an already large learning rate causes divergence and collapse (probe 78).
Stepping back from an unstable learning rate restores training (probe 63).
Wider networks make faster progress when training is learning-rate limited (probes 90, 93, 99).
Extra layers add capacity and effective step size in under-trained low-LR runs (probes 48, 53, 59).
Smaller batches give more updates, compensating for a too-small learning rate (probe 33).

Very narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening them helps more than widening already-wide ones (probe 82).

raw:
Hypotheses are drawn from the 100 single-seed probes and from standard MLP/Adam behaviour. Each probe used one seed, so the evidence for each one is suggestive rather than conclusive.

1. **Alpha down when alpha is high: effect higher.** Lowering alpha from 1 gave about +5 to +13 points on every dataset (probes 3 and 16). At that strength the penalty underfits the network, so relaxing it helps a lot.
2. **Alpha up when alpha is high: effect lower.** Raising an already large penalty should push the network further into underfitting.
3. **Learning rate up when learning rate is low: effect higher.** At 1e-5, a step up gave +2 to +10 points (probes 62 and 73). With such a tiny rate, 243 epochs is not enough to finish training.
4. **Learning rate up when learning rate is high: effect lower.** Probe 78 dropped 8 to 34 points as the run became unstable.
5. **Learning rate down when learning rate is high: effect higher.** Probe 63 gained 14 points on segment. Stepping back from an unstable rate restores training.
6. **Width up when learning rate is low: effect higher.** Probes 90, 93 and 99 were positive on all three datasets. Wider networks make faster progress when the run is under-trained.
7. **Depth up when learning rate is low: effect higher.** Probes 48, 53 and 59 were mostly clearly positive.
8. **Batch size down when learning rate is low: effect higher.** Probe 33 gained 1 to 16 points. Smaller batches mean more updates, which offsets the slow learning rate.
9. **Batch size up when learning rate is low: effect lower.** Larger batches mean fewer updates, which further starves a run that is already slow.
10. **Width up when width is low: effect higher.** Probe 82 was positive on all three datasets. Capacity is the bottleneck at 16 units.
